_comment: Golden set for contact resolution: job URL -> employer -> domain, and company-name matching. Every row is a REAL case from this account, including every bug that shipped. Negative cases are the point: a set of happy paths passed all four shipped bugs. Runner: tests/test_eval_resolution.py

SHIPPED BUG: all 3 candidates dropped, incl. the CEO. Apollo files avathongov.com people under the org name 'Avathon', and Government is not a corporate descriptor — but Apollo returned them FOR that domain, so the name is ambiguity, not proof they work elsewhere
the same names WITHOUT the domain search still reject — this fix must not loosen name matching
a wrong work-email domain is near-proof and must still reject even when Apollo returned them for our domain
Government is NOT a corporate descriptor — these stay different names; the Avathon fix works on evidence, not on widening this

SHIPPED BUG, the real one: Avathon was SparkCognition and kept the mail domain. avathongov.com was GUESSED from the careers host, so @sparkcognition.com contradicts an inference, not a fact. Three real employees incl. the CEO were dropped for it
the guard that must survive: when the domain came from Apollo it is evidence, and a contradicting work email is still near-proof
a guess that turns out RIGHT is still positive evidence

shipped bug: .edu was missing from _TLD_LABELS, so careersearch.stanford.edu resolved to the employer 'Edu' — third instance after 'Ats' and 'Hr', and the one that reached a real resume and cover letter

shipped bug: the Workday tenant slug ouryahoo.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com stored the employer as 'Ouryahoo'. Apollo has no such company and truthfully returned 0 contacts; company_lookup('Yahoo') returns six orgs. Refined only when the posting's own text names it as a whole word — 'OurCrowd' must never become 'Crowd'.

shipped bug: derive_company step 1 applies _company_owns_the_posting to a STORED company, but step 4 (_host_label) did not — so google.com/about/careers resolved to no employer at all and contact discovery never ran. Written down in Lessons 20 and only half implemented. After the fix: 8 known connections + 4 exact-title peers + 4 recruiters.
the other side of the same rule: a board showing SOMEBODY ELSE's job must still resolve to no employer, or outreach goes to the board's own staff

shipped bug: Oracle Recruiting Cloud pods carry the employer NOWHERE. Resolved to 'Oraclecloud', which became the domain, and Apollo has oraclecloud.com filed under the City of Atlanta — five Atlanta city employees found, four emailed. None is the only honest answer from this URL.

the fix's own failure mode: adding oraclecloud to the board hosts made _host_label fall back to labels[0] and return 'Eohh' — the pod, not the hospital. The first label is the tenant on Workday and breezy, and is meaningless here.
same Oracle product (/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/) on the employer's OWN domain — the vendor rule must key on the host, not the path

shipped bug: an ad-network redirect described the DISTRIBUTOR. Found by generating a real draft (Lessons 42) that read 'I applied for the Marketing Science Consultant position at Recruitics' next to a metacareers.com link. Fifth in the Ats/Hr/Edu/Ouryahoo/Oraclecloud family; 3 contacts stored, 0 emailed.
description: Meta is seeking a Marketing Science Consultant to join the team.
domain_note: was 'metacareers.com' until the careers-suffix split. This row's assertion is the UNWRAP - the employer is Meta and not Recruitics - and the domain was only ever a record of what the code then did. A careers host is not a mail domain; service.py recovers meta.com by corroboration, verified live.

why: the fix's OWN failure mode: blocking the vendor name alone yielded the employer 'Jsv3' — the pod code one label to the left, exactly how the Oracle fix reproduced its bug before landing. Hence _OPAQUE_TENANT_HOSTS as well as _BOARD_HOSTS.

shipped bug: jobs.jobvite.com/legalzoom -> the ATS vendor. 3 contacts stored at @jobvite.com with confidence:high against a LegalZoom role, 0 emailed. Sixth in the Ats/Hr/Edu/Ouryahoo/Oraclecloud/Recruitics family and the one that ended the blocklist approach.
description: About LegalZoom. LegalZoom is on a mission to help people navigate the legal system with confidence. LegalZoom was founded in 2001 and today LegalZoom serves millions.

why: live row: q2ebanking.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/Q2 -> 'Q2ebanking', which is nobody. The posting says 'Why Join Q2? Q2 is a leading provider of digital banking'. A two-character tenant slot has to stay eligible; the corroboration threshold is what keeps it from matching a fiscal quarter.
description: Why Join Q2? Q2 is a leading provider of digital banking and lending solutions. At Q2 we serve banks and credit unions. Q2 is hiring in Austin.

why: live row: careers.peak6.com hosts the posting but the Workday tenant is apexfintechsolutions and the posting opens 'WHO WE ARE Apex Fintech Solutions (Apex) powers innovation'. The hiring entity is the subsidiary, not the parent brand whose careers site carries it. 8 contacts had been stored at peak6.com, 0 emailed.
description: WHO WE ARE Apex Fintech Solutions powers innovation and the future of digital wealth management. Apex Fintech Solutions builds custody and clearing. Join Apex Fintech Solutions.

why: the challenger's OWN failure mode: allowing the first three path segments came one coincidence away from renaming the PEAK6 row to 'Technology'. Only the host's first label and the FIRST path segment are tenant slots.
description: We work in technology. Technology is the core of our technology practice. Technology, technology, technology.

why: shipped bug, live row, 3 searches and 0 contacts: www.schwabjobs.com resolved to the employer 'Schwab' correctly and to the domain 'schwabjobs.com', which Apollo maps to CHARLES SCHWAB INDIA - a different legal entity with no product managers indexed. Titled search returned 0; the widen-to-whole-company fallback returned 5 people in a location OUTREACH_EXCLUDE_LOCATIONS drops. A careers host is the employer's and is still not where anyone's email is. With no domain, company_lookup('Schwab') returns Charles Schwab first.
description: Schwab is a leader in financial services. At Schwab we champion clients. Join Schwab and help us reimagine wealth management. Schwab offers a modern workplace.

why: the same rule on the case that USED to be asserted True. Rejecting metacareers.com is not a loss: confirm_employer_domain('Meta') corroborates and returns meta.com, which is where Meta's people actually have addresses. Verified live - both hosts return identical people, so nothing is given up and the mail domain is the honest one.
description: Meta builds technology that helps people connect. Meta is seeking a product manager. At Meta you will work across teams.
